proposal.name: Rebuild closed modeled drafts on retry

issue_plan.name: Rebuild closed modeled drafts on retry
issue_plan.summary: A writer's retry posted after a person closes a failed modeled draft will build the same ratified statements again in a new pull request. The protocol amendment also removes its unused decision follow-up, and the recovery amendment includes #706's publication handoff, with both checked within their existing CI jobs. One plumbing change then connects the closed-draft retry to the factory, its posts, dashboard cards and /act, and deploys every watcher before the dashboard. Retries posted while a modeled draft is open still request a watch, and closing it never starts a build. The issues explain how to rebuild or revise, update decisions and documentation, and leave #706's plumbing in its existing issue.

issues.title: Authorize retrying a closed modeled draft in the issue protocol
issues.body:
Project: factory/protocol

The owner chose option 1 of #945 on 19 November 2026: after a person closes a modeled build's failed draft without merging it, a writer's retry builds the same ratified statements again, from their ratification, in a new pull request. This covers a draft left by failure of the factory's own gate and that draft after an earlier retry watched it and CI's gate failed. Closing the pull request alone must not start a build.

Amend the existing issue protocol to authorize this path. Today OthersClose clears the failure and enters closed, Retry requires failed, and Rebuild requires the factory's own gate failure. Represent enough provenance to retain the eligible failed draft and its ratified proposal across watch, CI failure and closure. Distinguish this case from a merged pull request or an unrelated closed pull request; merely being closed must not confer rebuild authority. A retry posted after the human close must work whether the watcher has already reported that close or discovers it while handling the command. The ordering is the retry's posting time against GitHub's record of when the pull request closed, not the factory's close report. A retry posted while the draft was open requests a watch; if the person closes the draft before that retry is answered, answer it without a build and say that another retry builds again. Model that distinction without adding clocks or unbounded history.

The authorized transition returns to ratified with the same proposal and ratification. Clear the earlier pull request's head, CI result, lock, scope and merge state, and reset the stopped-build count as an explicit retry does. Only a human with repository write access can request it. A retry must stay attached to its eligible build rather than authorize a later attempt. While a modeled draft remains open, retry still watches that pull request. Preserve the existing plan-draft Rebuild path, stopped-build retries, revision and new-ratification path, and all current-head, scope, lock and trusted-base merge requirements.

Explicitly amend the pinned RebuildsOwnFailures guarantee and the RebuildAfterCI known bug to admit this closed-draft case while continuing to reject rebuilding an open pull request merely because CI failed. Keep BuildStartsClean meaningful. Update IssueProtocol.tla, the Go core and contracts, explorer and project README together. Include witnesses for own-gate failure then close then retry, and own-gate failure then watch then CI failure then close then retry, followed by a successful build, another failed draft or a stopped build. Include a witness for a pending watch whose draft closes before its answer, with no rebuild until a later retry. Include counterexamples for unauthorized retry, using the new modeled-draft rebuild path without an eligible close and subsequent retry, replacing merged work and retaining the old pull request's evidence. Preserve the ordinary watcher API and its existing behavior until the integration issue connects the new path.

This amendment also fulfills D-0465's instruction to remove the protocol's unused decision follow-up when the protocol is next amended for its own reasons. Remove the follow-up constants and bounds, variables, statements, Go core and contracts, explorer branches and tests from factory/protocol, as #891 did. Keep Next's grouping of the remaining actions and the explorer's report of each group's distinct outcomes, including successful self-loops and a refusal only when the whole group refuses; do not restore the slower enumeration of every leaf attempt. Keep this removal inside factory/protocol: nothing in internal/ or cmd/ uses that follow-up code, the ordinary watcher API remains usable, and factory/decision-followup stays as it is. Make the project's README, including its statement table and ratification account, match the amended lock; its table has lacked the follow-up statements since #428. Cite D-0465 and D-0293 in the amendment.

Keep the encoding finite and forgetful: use small finite sets and booleans, with no new counters, sequences or per-attempt sets. Clear new provenance wherever no statement reads it, including at a merge, a new draft or a rebuild; in particular, do not retain a closed-draft flag through someone else's merge when it serves no remaining statement. Before ratification, the proposal must report TLC's distinct states at the ratified bounds and one size larger, before and after the complete amendment. Today's grouped protocol has 132,486 and 940,960 states respectively. If the proposal exceeds 132,486 at the ratified bounds, or exceeds two and a half times today's count at either size, say so and explain why at the top of the proposal for the owner to decide before ratifying. The discussion's sketches are sizing estimates, not measurements of the final amendment.

The complete verification gate must fit the existing 40-minute project CI job. The pull request must compare its CI job time with today's 13.1–22.8 minutes over 54 runs from 13–19 November 2026, median 17.1, and compare its receipt's steps recorded with today's 1,503,852. Retain the receipt and TLC resource history showing that no conformance window ran out of memory and split, the failure mode reported in #659. Include all checks in that job and report measured evidence, not state counts alone.

This is a modeled amendment under D-0064 and D-0105, refining D-0202/D-0209 and the retry boundary in D-0191/D-0218, and removing D-0293's follow-up under D-0465. Inspect their dependents before drafting it. Obtain the owner's ratification of the changed statements through the normal amendment flow before changing pinned statements or ratified.lock; ratifying this issue plan alone does not ratify those statements. Run the complete factory/protocol verification gate, including model checks, witnesses, known bugs, Go proof and conformance. At merge, record the amendment with the decisions CLI and keep SPEC.md, README.md and docs/factory.md accurate under AGENTS.md, using a merger follow-up where factory scope requires it, before the next issue starts. Describe the amended core without claiming the watcher already uses the new path.

issues.title: Recover a rebuild requested after a person closes a modeled draft
issues.body:
Project: factory/recovery

After the protocol amendment for #945 merges, amend the recovery core for the same authorized retry: a human writer asks to build the existing ratified statements again after a person closes a failed modeled draft without merging it, including a draft previously watched by a retry and subsequently failed by CI. The existing recovery model cannot take this path: GiveRetry excludes closed pull requests and previously watched drafts, and a predecessor closed before replacement intent is recorded produces an answer without a build.

Represent this new retry authority explicitly, with enough failed-draft and closure provenance to distinguish it from ordinary closure. Record which retry starts the new attempt and which closed draft it replaces in state every watcher can recover before answering the retry and starting its build. A human close stays a human close; the factory must neither close that pull request again nor pretend it retired it. The new attempt owns its run, code publication, pull request and answer, and preserves the ratification. It may succeed, stop partway or leave another failed draft, which can in turn be closed and retried. An earlier watch of the closed draft must neither block the new attempt nor supply watch or gate authority for its successor.

Preserve one answer per command and build, one run and at most one pull request per build, and at most one open pull request for the work. Only the lease holder takes effects. A superseded run can be recorded only as its own result and cannot publish for the successor. A merged predecessor cannot be replaced. Keep the existing plan-draft replacement rules, including recording intent before the factory closes an open draft and answering without a build when someone closed that plan draft before the record. A watched modeled draft remains unreplaceable while open; the new authority requires the person's close and a retry posted after it, ordered by GitHub's closure time rather than the factory's report. A watch requested while the draft was open, but still unanswered when it closes, is answered without a build; only a later retry supplies rebuild authority. Keep stopped-build retries and existing watch/readiness/merge behavior.

Include #706's pending recovery transition in this same amendment. Someone can move a build's branch between the factory's code push and completion of publication, including before the pull request opens. The factory must never publish, ready or merge the moved head without checking it as it would its own build commit. Model a handoff for the unchecked moved head: answer the build exactly once with a report for a person, stop publication of that head, and allow a writer's retry to build again as after any stopped build. Preserve that handoff across crashes and a second watcher, with no automatic publication on later polls and no reuse of the old commit's evidence for the moved head. The issue protocol already permits this handoff as StopBuild; this step adds the recovery authority, not another protocol amendment.

Update WatcherRecovery.tla, the proved Go core and contracts, explorer and project README. Explicitly qualify the existing rule that a watched draft is never replaced and the closed-before-intent outcome, rather than silently weakening their statements. Keep all four existing liveness properties, CommandsAnswered, BuildsAnswered, GatedPullRequestsSettled and WatchedDraftsSettled, under the five existing fairness statements, FairAcquire, FairExpire, FairAct, FairFinishRun and FairDropRun. Eligible retries and their builds, including #706's handoff and retry, must eventually be answered across crashes and a second watcher. Add witnesses for rebuilding an already closed failed draft, rebuilding after an earlier watch, recovering each interrupted replacement stage, repeated failed attempts and a stopped replacement. Also witness a pending watch answered after the person's close without a build, and #706's moved-head handoff followed by its retry and new build. Add a known bug that publishes the moved head using the old build's authority. Add known bugs for duplicate answers or runs, reusing the predecessor's gate or result, replacing merged work, bypassing the required retry/record and opening a successor while the predecessor is still open. Preserve the exported operations and defaults the current watcher uses until integration; this amendment changes no watcher behavior. #706's plumbing stays in its own existing issue and builds on this amendment. At this step's merge, remove #706's Waits: line and record its dependency on this merged core; do not fold its watcher integration into step 3 of #945.

Keep the encoding finite and forgetful: small finite sets and booleans, with no new counters, sequences or per-attempt sets. Clear new provenance wherever no statement reads it, including at a merge, a new draft or a rebuild. Any flag needed to witness that the closed draft was previously watched must not keep irrelevant history for later attempts. Before ratification, the proposal must report TLC's distinct states at the ratified bounds and one size larger, before and after both the closed-draft retry and #706 changes together. Today's recovery model has 50,941 and 383,368 states respectively. If the proposal exceeds two and a half times today's count at either size, say so and explain why at the top of the proposal for the owner to decide before ratifying. The discussion's sketches are sizing estimates, not measurements of the final amendment.

The complete verification gate must fit the existing 40-minute project CI job; #659 records an earlier recovery amendment whose replay outgrew it. The pull request must compare its CI job time with today's 5.9–10.2 minutes over the 13–19 November 2026 comparison period, median 8.0, and compare its receipt's steps recorded with today's 3,157,617. Retain the receipt and TLC resource history showing that no conformance window ran out of memory and split. Include all checks in that job and report measured evidence, not state counts alone.

Basis: #945's selected behavior and discussion, #706's publication handoff, the preceding protocol amendment, D-0069/D-0074, D-0203/D-0210, D-0218 and D-0225. Inspect dependents and have the owner ratify the statement changes through the normal amendment flow before updating pinned statements or ratified.lock. Run the complete factory/recovery gate, including safety and liveness checks, witnesses, known bugs, Go proof and conformance. At merge, record the amendment with the decisions CLI and keep SPEC.md, README.md and docs/factory.md accurate, with any scope-required merger follow-up completed before integration. The documentation must distinguish core support from the watcher behavior still awaiting integration.

issues.title: Build closed modeled drafts again and offer the same action everywhere
issues.body:
Kind: plumbing

Connect the closed-draft retry behavior of the two ratified #945 core amendments to internal/factory and internal/dashboard, with GitHub closure evidence supplied through internal/github. #706's moved-head watcher integration remains in its own issue. The owner chose that a writer's retry after a person closes a failed modeled draft builds the same ratified statements again from their ratification, on a new branch and in a new pull request, without another proposal or ratification. This must work both directly after the factory's own gate failure and after a retry watched that draft and CI's gate failed. While the modeled draft is open, retry continues to watch it.

Update thread/marker interpretation, command dispatch, closure handling, rebuild logic and both core adapters so an eligible human close remains retryable. Preserve the failed build's identity and ratification through subsequent watch, CI-failure and closed posts. Recognize existing eligible histories from their durable posts, including histories written before this change; do not infer eligibility from an arbitrary closed marker or silently substitute an older proposal when evidence cannot be read. Handle a retry posted after the person closed the draft but before the watcher reported the close, as well as one posted after that report. Rebuild authority requires the retry to have been posted after GitHub's recorded closure time for that pull request; the factory's close-report time is not the boundary. Read and carry that closure time through the GitHub adapter and fixtures. A retry posted while the draft was open requests a watch. If the person closes it before that retry is answered, answer once without building and explain that another retry now builds the same statements again. Closure alone starts nothing, including when a watch is pending, and stale or queued retries cannot rebuild a later attempt. Do not grant rebuild authority when closure or ordering evidence cannot be established. Route the transition and effects through the amended cores.

Find and validate the commit containing the same modeled ratification, including the retained source commit on later attempts. Extend the modeled runBuild/worktree path, which currently starts only from origin/<branch>, to create the retry's branch from that commit rather than from the failed draft's code. Keep project/branch validation and both inline and saved-proposal handling. Give each retry a durable replacement record, its own build/run identity and its own pull request; leave the human-closed draft and its work available to read. Run the normal modeled synthesis, verification and review, and apply the existing publication and trusted-base merge rules to the successor. A new failure may leave another draft, and a stopped replacement retains enough information for the next retry. If the ratification cannot be recovered, answer once with an actionable explanation and the revise/new-ratification route, expose that limitation on its card, and avoid an endless build or poll failure.

Make the factory's failed-build post, CI-failure post, closed post, retry answer and refused-revision guidance describe the actual actions: retry watches an open modeled draft; closing an eligible failed draft and then retrying rebuilds the same statements; revising changes the proposal and requires ratification. An ineligible retry must explain the available next step rather than only say nothing failed. Keep commands and their meanings in the unclipped closing of long posts. Update the dashboard's server-derived Takes and retry copy, public and /act cards, confirmation, posted feedback and history to match. An eligible closed draft offers rebuilding and revision; unavailable ratification offers revision. /act must accept only the commands its current card permits and send the existing retry command. History must attribute the earlier close to the person, not claim the factory closed it.

Acceptance tests must exercise the real factory poll/build/publication paths with controlled builders and GitHub/repository fixtures for both failure histories and both close-report timings: a retry posted after GitHub recorded the close but before the factory reported it, and one posted after that report. Beside those cases, cover a retry posted while the modeled draft was open, then a human close before the factory answers it: no new build, run or pull request; one answer explaining that another retry rebuilds; and a subsequent retry that does rebuild. Exercise this pending-watch case for both failure histories, and a close with no retry. Assert the ordering against GitHub's closure timestamp, independently of the close post, and cover unavailable closure evidence without granting rebuild authority. Assert the unchanged ratified hash/lock, exact starting commit, distinct branch/run/pull request, fresh checks and review, one command answer, and no reopening, readying or merging of the old draft. Cover a second failed draft closed and retried, a stopped replacement, an older eligible history, a missing ratification on a fresh clone, merged or ineligible predecessors, unauthorized commands and a retry queued before a later failure. Interrupt each new durable effect and resume with another watcher to demonstrate no duplicated run, post or pull request and no stale publication. Retain regressions for open modeled drafts watching again, plan-draft replacement including its close-before-record rule, ordinary CI retries, issue closure and trusted-base handling. Test served dashboard state, rendered action/guidance, /act acceptance/refusal and posted feedback for the same scenarios, including clipped posts. Update existing pinned acceptance expectations only for the explicitly changed closed-modeled-draft behavior and its guidance.

Keep SPEC.md, README.md and docs/factory.md current in this change, within the README's 400-line limit. Record #945's selected behavior and the amended boundaries using the decisions CLI and the repository's ratified-plan rules; complete any decision-writing merger follow-up before moving on. Basis: the two preceding amendments, D-0156, D-0191, D-0218, D-0225 and D-0237/D-0238. Run the affected factory and dashboard tests and the required checks in AGENTS.md. This work overlaps #933 in internal/factory: whichever merges second must incorporate the first and check their combined behavior against the resulting base.

Merger work includes deployment. Steps 1 and 2 change no watcher behavior, and this integration is not complete on merge alone. Redeploy every watcher the factory runs from a build of main containing this change. Follow docs/factory.md's Draining and restarting procedure for each lease holder: time the rollout between long builds because a draining holder keeps new work waiting until admitted builds finish; send SIGUSR1, wait for the process to finish its work and exit and release its lease, then replace its binary and restart with the same flags and work directory. A staged successor needs its own binary and work directory. Verify that every running watcher is on a main build containing the change before deploying the dashboard, so its cards never offer a rebuild that a running watcher cannot take. Then post on #945 when retries began rebuilding eligible closed modeled drafts, with the deployed main revision and effective time. Complete this rollout and report as part of this issue's merger work.
